description: Document and asset generation engine. Reads pdf/pptx/docx/xlsx with the native engines (document_digest, pdf_extract, pptx_slide_text, docx_extract, xlsx_extract; opt-in local OCR for embedded images) and includes pptx_filter_slides for template-inheriting partial-update workflows.

invocation_contexts.note: This actuator has two op namespaces. Choose based on where the step is written.

from_top_level_pipeline.note: The runner splits domain:action, loads media-actuator, and wraps the step in a single-step sub-pipeline.

from_media_actuator_examples_or_nested_s.note: Used inside media-actuator/examples/ or steps passed directly to executePipeline. No domain prefix needed.

capture.note: Extract per-slide text from a PPTX in presentation order (position; slide_index stays the slideN.xml number) with hidden, shapes_text (newline-separated paragraphs), tables, notes_text, image_parts and concatenated. Set params.ocr=true or params.ocr.enabled=true to OCR slide images through the local OCR router; EMF/WMF are rasterized via LibreOffice first and unreadable images are listed in ocr_skipped.
Extract full PPTX design protocol (slides + master theme + raw passthrough) into context. Set params.ocr=true or params.ocr.enabled=true to attach OCR results for slide images.

Extract a PdfDesignProtocol with the native PDF engine (per-page text merged with pdf-parse text, positioned elements, placed images extracted to a per-document dir under active/shared/tmp/native-pdf/images/). Set params.ocr=true or params.ocr={ language, mode, min_area_ratio } to OCR each page's placed images (tables, charts; images under 3% of the page are skipped) into page.imageOcr.

Read pdf/pptx/xlsx/docx/html/txt/md/csv/tsv/json/yaml into LLM-ready Markdown through the shared document reader (@agent/core/document-reader — same output as `pnpm kyberion read` and ingest) (tables, headings, line breaks; docx pictures as _[image: media/x.png]_ markers; small csv/tsv as tables; json pretty-printed). params.ocr OCRs embedded images of pdf/pptx/docx; reader warnings land in <export_as>_warnings.

Extract a DocxDesignProtocol with the native docx reader. Pictures are written as files and referenced by drawing.imagePath (per-document dir under active/shared/tmp/native-docx/images/, or params.image_dir). Set params.embed_images=true for a self-contained design with inline base64 imageData.
Extract full XLSX design protocol (sheets + styles + raw passthrough) into context. Pass params.sheet / params.range / params.values_only for a slim values-only projection.
Read a JSON file into context.

Inspect the PPTX at path for the structural defects that make PowerPoint demand a repair: EMPTY_TXBODY, BROKEN_REL, DANGLING_RID, MISSING_CONTENT_TYPE, DUPLICATE_SLDID (errors) and ORPHAN_PART (any part unreachable from the package root), CHANGES_INFO_PRESENT, BROKEN_REL on NULL / #anchor placeholder targets (warnings). params.fail_on = error (default) | warn | never; the report { path, ok, issues[] } lands in export_as (default pptx_package_check).

Compare params.before and params.after (two .pptx paths) part by part: only_in_before / only_in_after, changed[] ordered by relevance (package structure, then slides/layouts/masters, then the rest) with LCS-aligned tag diffs, and summary { counts, significant_parts }. noise_only marks attribute-order, xmlns / mc:Ignorable, docProps/* and embedded font subset changes; params.parts filters by glob. Repair triage: diff your output against the PowerPoint-repaired copy; ignore noise_only parts; the first significant_parts (usually a slide or a .rels) show what the repair changed — fix that writer, then confirm with pptx_package_check.

transform.note: Select slide indices by owner labels from pptx_slide_text output.
Compare two extracted slide sets and report added, removed, changed, and unchanged slides.
Set a key in the pipeline context. Use to inject theme, content arrays, or config before merge_content.
Load a named theme from knowledge/public/design-patterns/media-templates/themes.json into active_theme.
Load a design pattern JSON into active_pattern.
Combine active_theme + active_pattern + content_data into last_pptx_design (or last_xlsx_design, etc.).
Derive a reusable theme from an extracted PPTX design (for master-theme reuse across decks).
Generate a narrative outline from a proposal brief.
Expand a storyline into per-slide content_data ready for merge_content.
Compile a canonical media brief into a render-ready design protocol.

Convert Kyberion report HTML (hero/h2/h3/p/.callout/table/.chip|.sev/ul/.kpis/.grpttl) into an editable last_pptx_design protocol, inheriting the HTML's :root design tokens. Source via params.html, params.path, or ctx channel (params.from). Pair with pptx_render.
Emit the in-page measurement script for browser:evaluate. Paired with deck_from_geometry (same geometry schema); params: aspect|canvas, viewport_px, font, deck_css.

Transcribe browser-measured layout geometry (from browser:evaluate) into an editable last_pptx_design protocol. Uses real wrap positions instead of estimating, so column widths match the report HTML. Pair with pptx_render.
Validate compiled PPTX layout diagnostics before any render; overflow requires explicit review-only opt-in.

MP-04: rasterize a rendered artifact and inspect it against the visual-review rubric. Reports only — a review that cannot run (missing rasterizer, denied egress, no vision channel) returns status=skipped with a reason and is never a pass.
Block delivery unless visual review completed with no outstanding errors.

MP-05: fix the media brief before production and record which decisions were stated by the operator versus inferred here. Carries the run-shape (review rounds, degraded-fallback and external-egress permissions) that downstream steps obey.

apply.note: Register a validated presentation preference profile in the media/design policy registry.

Render last_pptx_design to a .pptx file. Supports text, shape, image (imagePath or imageData), table, line, and smartart elements. For a rawParts protocol the original package is the baseline, so only new defects block. Writes pass the package gate: params.package_check = error (default; refuses structural defects this write introduces) | warn (log and write) | never; defects inherited from the source deck are written through with a logged warning.

Write a subset of slides from an existing PPTX by index (slideN.xml numbers, emitted in the given order); notes of kept slides are re-pointed, notes of dropped slides removed. Writes pass the package gate: params.package_check = error (default; refuses structural defects this write introduces) | warn (log and write) | never; defects inherited from the source deck are written through with a logged warning.

Text-replacement patch on an existing PPTX (simple find-replace). Writes pass the package gate: params.package_check = error (default; refuses structural defects this write introduces) | warn (log and write) | never; defects inherited from the source deck are written through with a logged warning.

Replace whole paragraphs (exact or contains match on the paragraph's combined run text); the new text lands in the first run. Writes pass the package gate: params.package_check = error (default; refuses structural defects this write introduces) | warn (log and write) | never; defects inherited from the source deck are written through with a logged warning.

Replace slide replace_index (1-based) of an existing deck (path) with slides[] generated from semantic blocks (lead, kpi_band, labeled_rows, stage_columns, card_row, trend_chart, bullets, columns) and write to out. The template slide's head shapes and layout are reused, subtitle_shape receives slides[i].subtitle, colours/fonts come from theme (object, theme JSON path or media theme id). The package is rewritten: fresh slide/relationship ids, notes on the first slide only, template comments not copied, changesInfo removed, and every part only the replaced slide used (media, charts and embedded workbooks, SmartArt, comments, ...) removed. Writes pass the package gate: params.package_check = error (default; refuses structural defects this write introduces) | warn (log and write) | never; defects inherited from the source deck are written through with a logged warning.
Write a context value to a file path.
